title: SIWATT M270-35A Technical Data Sheet
locator: pp. 1–2, magnetic properties, physical properties and 50 Hz curves
relevant_data: Density 7.69 kg/dm³ at 20 °C (typical). Electrical resistivity 42.2 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m (typical). At 50 Hz, total loss 1.08 W/kg at 1.0 T and 2.64 W/kg at 1.5 T (typical), with 2.70 W/kg guaranteed maximum at 1.5 T. Typical polarisation 1.60/1.69/1.80 T at 2500/5000/10000 A/m. Total-loss and magnetisation curves.
units: kg/dm³, Ω·m, W/kg, T, Hz, A/m, °C
evidence_limitations: Material sheet data. Curve uses polarisation J. No quasi-static loop family, matched frequency sweep, separate hysteresis coefficient or finished-core performance.

title: SIWATT Catalogue
locator: Fully processed grades, designation comparison and nominal thickness table
relevant_data: M270-35A designation and nominal 0.35 mm sheet gauge.
evidence_limitations: Catalogue sheet gauge. Actual steel thickness, coating, stack factor and finished lamination dimensions depend on the selected product and assembly.

title: Grain-oriented electrical steel powercore
relevant_data: Transformer use of grain-oriented steel. H125-35 is 0.35 mm with maximum total specific loss 1.25 W/kg at 1.7 T and 50 Hz.
evidence_limitations: Different grade, orientation and material test point. Context only. Provides no coefficient for SIWATT.

title: General Properties of Power Losses in Soft Ferromagnetic Materials
organisation: Giorgio Bertotti / IEEE Transactions on Magnetics
locator: Vol. 24, pp. 621–630, especially Section I, Eqs. (1)–(3)
relevant_data: Quasi-static hysteresis, classical and excess loss separation. Thin-sheet classical equation under sinusoidal magnetisation.
evidence_limitations: Equation and mechanism reference. Specimens do not provide SIWATT coefficients. IEEE gateway presented a JavaScript check. Published full text checked via https://sci.bban.top/pdf/10.1109/20.43994.pdf

title: Harmonization and Validation of Jiles–Atherton Static Hysteresis Models
relevant_data: A DC hysteresis loop measured for a 40 × 100 mm M270-35A steel sample. The paper compares measured and fitted loops and reports loop energy.
units: mm, T, A/m, J/m³ per cycle
evidence_limitations: Evidence for a specified test specimen. No fit over several measured amplitudes for the selected SIJ sheet.

title: Measurements and Modeling of Iron Losses in Guillotine and Laser Cut Soft-Magnetic Sheets
organisation: Gmyrek, Graffeo, Vaschetto and Cavagnino / IEEE Open Journal of Industry Applications / Politecnico di Torino
evidence_type: Institutional record for peer-reviewed original research
relevant_data: Confirms final citation (2025, vol. 6, pp. 663–675) and scope of three-component loss analysis with cutting effects.
evidence_limitations: Automated access to repository version-of-record PDF returned HTTP 403. Use MAG-4 for inspected methods and data coverage.

title: Measurements and Modeling of Iron Losses in Guillotine and Laser Cut Soft-Magnetic Sheets
organisation: Gmyrek, Graffeo, Vaschetto and Cavagnino / accepted IEEE author manuscript
evidence_type: Accepted primary research manuscript hosted by ResearchGate
relevant_data: M270-35A strips of 0.35 mm, measured over 5–500 Hz and 0.1–1.5 T. Hysteresis energy estimated from a zero-frequency extrapolation of p/f at fixed induction. Width- and cut-dependent fitted parameters.
units: mm, Hz, T, W/kg, J/kg per cycle
evidence_limitations: Author manuscript. Specimen width, cut method and rolling direction affect transferability. No confirmed match to selected SIWATT sheet or E–I assembly.

title: Electromagnetics and Applications, 6.013 Course Notes
organisation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology / MIT OpenCourseWare
relevant_data: Faraday induction and common-flux turns ratio. The sinusoidal RMS voltage expression in the framework is derived from these principles.
evidence_limitations: Idealised reference. Gives no validation of winding regulation or core saturation for the proposed design.

title: Copper Wire Tables, NBS Handbook 100
organisation: US National Bureau of Standards / NIST archival publication
locator: Section 1.3 and Appendix 5, International Standard of Resistance for Copper
relevant_data: Reference standard annealed copper conductivity of 58 m/(Ω·mm²), giving approximately 1.7241 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m. Reference resistance temperature coefficient 0.00393 per °C at 20 °C.
evidence_limitations: Reference material and temperature. Actual wire resistance, conductor size, insulation and winding temperature are separate inputs.
